description: Astronomy, Latin, architecture, robotics, Apollo history, science fiction, classical music, orbital mechanics, Elizabethan conspiracy, neuroscience and language carry the quiz from early 2025 into the first months of 2026.

s10e01.description: Scintillation explains why stars appear to twinkle and gives the episode a beautifully technical title. Astronomy turns a familiar night-sky observation into precise science, while the rest of the ladder performs its own less attractive flickering of certainty.

s10e02.description: ‘Pro bono’ brings compact Latin into everyday professional language and the question ladder. The episode makes familiar phrases feel newly examinable, because apparently using an expression for years is no guarantee of knowing exactly what it means.

s10e03.description: Portmeirion provides architecture, Wales and a touch of surreal visual character in one memorable place. The episode wanders through broader knowledge, but a village that already looks slightly improbable is ideally suited to becoming quiz trivia.

s10e04.description: The Eden Project brings giant biomes and ambitious environmental design into the hot seat. Architecture, science and geography meet on a ladder where an enormous greenhouse complex is somehow among the easier things to visualise.

s10e05.description: ‘End effector’ gives robotics a term that sounds vaguely ominous until it is explained. Engineering supplies the episode’s best piece of specialist vocabulary, surrounded by questions that make the human answering mechanism look comparatively unreliable.

s10e06.description: Lunar Module Eagle lands in the episode with one of space exploration’s most recognisable machine names. Apollo-era history anchors a broad ladder where remembering humanity’s giant leaps still depends on several very small factual steps.

s10e07.description: Arthur Dent brings bathrobes, bureaucracy and cosmic inconvenience into the question set. Science fiction supplies the episode’s most personable reference while the wider ladder remains almost as indifferent to human comfort as the universe he inhabits.

s10e08.description: ‘Also Sprach Zarathustra’ gives the episode a monumental musical title familiar far beyond the concert hall. Classical culture meets cinema and general knowledge, with a piece everyone recognises proving rather fewer people can confidently name.

s10e09.description: Perturbation turns orbital mechanics into one elegant scientific headache. Gravitational influence gives the episode its technical centre while the wider ladder repeatedly perturbs contestants’ own trajectories away from comfortable certainty.

s10e10.description: The Babington Plot brings Elizabethan espionage and conspiracy into the hot seat. Codes, intrigue and political history give the episode narrative energy, while the surrounding ladder reminds us that treason is easier to follow with multiple-choice options.

s10e11.description: The hypothalamus gives neuroscience its compact starring role. A tiny region of the brain becomes a large quiz concern, surrounded by a ladder that would be much easier if the organ being tested came with a built-in answer key.

s10e12.description: Serendipity gives the episode a word for fortunate accidental discovery. It is a charming concept for a quiz where success occasionally resembles exactly that, although the ladder continues to insist on calling it knowledge.

s10e13.description: Precognition brings knowledge of the future into a programme devoted to proving how unreliable knowledge of the present can be. The paranormal concept gives the episode a neat identity while the ladder remains stubbornly resistant to prophecy.

s10e14.description: The ornithopter gives flight a wonderfully mechanical imitation of birds. Engineering and imagination meet in one distinctive word, while the episode’s broader questions demonstrate that humans can copy wings more readily than they can organise memory.

s10e15.description: Velociraptor brings prehistoric speed and pop-cultural menace into the quiz. Paleontology supplies an instantly recognisable creature, though the episode still finds ways to make familiarity with dinosaurs less useful than childhood enthusiasm promised.

s10e16.description: Frangipane gives the episode almond-filled culinary precision. Baking terminology becomes serious quiz business for a moment, proving that pastry knowledge can stand beside science, history and literature without displaying the slightest inferiority complex.

s10e17.description: The moons of Uranus send the episode into the outer Solar System. Astronomy provides a wonderfully named family of worlds while the question ladder makes planetary distances seem simple compared with retrieving the correct fact from memory.
